claim: Big-blind calls can be wider because the posted blind improves the price and the BB often closes the preflop action.
interpretation: The relevant comparison is call EV versus the loss from folding the blind, with actual equity realisation and rake included.
assumptions: The action closes or nearly closes after Hero
The hand has some postflop playability
exceptions: High rake, large open sizes, strong early-position ranges or poor realisation can remove marginal calls
rake_or_structure_notes: Rake can turn marginal BB calls from acceptable to folds
notes: No exact chart boundary is claimed.

claim: Small-blind passive calls are structurally more expensive because the SB pays a worse price, remains out of position and leaves the BB able to squeeze.
interpretation: A passive SB call must include the probability of not reaching the flop after a BB squeeze and the cost of future out-of-position realisation.
assumptions: No special passive-BB read removes squeeze risk
exceptions: Some flats can survive when the BB is weak/passive or a versatile hand benefits from keeping weaker ranges in
rake_or_structure_notes: Winning preflop through 3-betting can avoid paying rake in some structures
notes: 3-bet-or-fold is taught as a useful default, not an absolute law.

claim: The same flop can require materially different c-bet strategies versus an SB caller and a BB caller because their preflop source ranges have different shapes.
interpretation: Board texture must be interpreted through the source range. Blind identity remains strategically relevant after the flop.
assumptions: SB and BB use broadly different baseline calling structures
No strong opponent-specific evidence collapses the difference
exceptions: A specific SB who repeatedly over-calls can reach the flop wider than the baseline prior suggests

claim: Raw equity is not enough to justify a blind defence; position, domination, squeeze exposure, rake and future betting determine how much equity can actually be realised.
interpretation: The trainer should ask about realisation explicitly instead of framing defence as a simple equity-versus-range comparison.
assumptions: The hand is not all-in preflop
exceptions: At very low SPR some realisation problems shrink because fewer future decisions remain
rake_or_structure_notes: Rake lowers realised value of marginal calls
